about: The short state of the project. Read it first; DESIGN.md has the detail and the evidence. Update it when a milestone, a decision or a dead end lands.

milestones.status: building: waves 1-3 and M4-10 merged (M4-01, -02, -03, -04, -05, -05a, -06, -10; each reviewed, CI green end to end in Ubuntu 26.04); M4-00b's CUDA 13 spike passed on the 5070; next M4-07 (the release), then the full review, M4-08
milestones.what: a release the friend can use on his Windows PC, running in WSL2: a guided WSL setup, a one-line install, a Start-menu shortcut, a local UI, tested on his PC
milestones.plan: docs/work-orders/M4-00-plan.md: v0.1 is a guide to set up WSL, install.sh fetched from the pre-release and checked by hash (uv lanes cu132/cu126/cpu, allin1's own Python, Node, autochart with its models and its CUDA 13 provider, doctor.json, a .wslconfig with Windows' RAM minus 4 GB, a Start-menu shortcut), device checks with the CPU fallback shown, the local UI in WSL opened in the Windows browser (drop, options, progress with cancel, the static preview, zip and install into the Windows Songs folder), diagnostics, and CI end to end in ubuntu:26.04. Native Windows and the rest are M4-99; the native plan is commit f9f9377 and M4-00's appendix.
risks: peak RAM with CUDA inside 12 GB of WSL memory (a 16 GB PC) is unmeasured: on the CPU the tree peaked at 10.1 GB, allin1's runner 7.8 GB; M4-08 measures it with memory=12GB, swap 8 GB absorbs short peaks, and under 11 GB of WSL memory allin1 is left out (librosa sections)

autochart's CUDA provider in WSL needs CUDA 13 libraries (cublas 13, cudart 13, nvrtc 13, cufft 12, curand 10, cuDNN 9): the cu132 lane's wheels plus nvidia-curand hold them, and in the dev container the provider loaded past all of them (only the driver's libcuda.so.1 was missing); never run on a GPU (eval/gpu.sh's earlier runs used CUDA 12 libraries), so M4-00b (packaging/spike/cuda13-provider.sh, the owner's 5070, about 20 min) must pass before wave 1 ends; a driver under 580 leaves the guitar on the CPU

the Start-menu shortcut under Smart App Control: a .lnk written from WSL has no Mark of the Web and targets the signed wsl.exe, so it should run; untested until M4-08 (fallback: open Ubuntu, type songcharter)
the Windows browser reaches the server through WSL's localhost forwarding (default on); the server checks it from Windows with curl.exe and falls back to WSL's own address
decisions: route: WSL2, not native Windows (the owner, 2026-11-03): the friend's PC has Smart App Control on, which blocks unsigned DLLs and Python modules with no per-app exception; Linux programs in WSL2 are outside it, and onnxruntime-node's Linux build gives the guitar CUDA again
delivery: a GitHub pre-release on neb882/song-charting (the owner)
licence: MIT for songcharter's own code, LICENSE on main (the owner); NOTICE lists the third parties
uninstall: the guide offers wsl --unregister Ubuntu as the complete uninstall, with a warning to use it only if that Ubuntu holds nothing else (the owner, 2026-11-03)

lyrics (M4-10, DESIGN 2.15): `--lyrics FILE` / Options.lyrics; the friend pastes the text, songcharter never looks lyrics up or transcribes; the aligner is torchaudio's English 960 h large CTC bundle with a star before every line, chosen by measurement on the six references' 1,277 human-timed words (0.915 within 250 ms on the stems; the multilingual bundle 0.854, ctc-forced-aligner 0.812); the text goes into notes.chart only, every report counts it

golden.status: done 2026-11-03 (branch golden), with the review's four fixes: --rerun on both runs (diff fails otherwise, and on an engine whose kept output is another commit's), the output folder cleared before any check, an engine run unasked stops the run (exit 2), exit 2/3 for bad input/bugs
golden.what: python -m eval.golden run builds the seven reference songs with songcharter chart (every level, 1 take, CPU) and records per part and difficulty the onsets, scan-chart's track hash and score.py's F1; diff OLD NEW --expect PARTS flags every other change UNEXPECTED (exit 1). DESIGN 3.6, eval/README.md; the commands are in eval/README.md (Golden charts), which docs/PIPELINE.md's release gate and sc-inspector use; a run takes the heavy-job lock (tools/heavy.sh).
golden.baseline: main at 656991d (--rerun guitar): eval/baseline/summary.json, committed (hashes and F1s, no audio); the first, at 11615e2, in <scratchpad>/golden/base. The kept work folders are in <scratchpad>/golden/work, made at 11615e2, so the guitar is rerun on both sides since M4-02 changed engines/autochart.py. Environment in the dev container: EVAL_DATA=<scratchpad>/eval SONGCHARTER_GOLDEN=<scratchpad>/golden, plus SONGCHARTER_SCAN_CHART, SONGCHARTER_AUTOCHART=<scratchpad>/eval/tools/autochart and SONGCHARTER_ALLIN1_PYTHON=<scratchpad>/research/timing/venv2/bin/python. <scratchpad> is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/5307d417-c453-5e74-8f13-b43b2df06ab1/scratchpad. Rebuilding it elsewhere: eval/README.md, 'Rebuilding the dev machine'.
golden.cost: cold (a kept folder made, stems hard-linked): 474-1081 s a song, 80 min for the set, the guitar take most of it; warm: 44-76 s a song, 6.5 min for the set (CPU, 2 threads)

dead_ends.what: filling sparse guitar stretches from pick-noise strumming
dead_ends.why: held-out precision 0.22 (6/27); an audio-free baseline did as well (10/39); 16th-note detection 0/22. No fill built.

dead_ends.what: solos by the stems rule (vocals quiet, guitar loud)
dead_ends.why: it rejects the real Car Seat Headrest solos (vocal stem active 0.56-0.95 of their frames); the default is now allin1's solo label
+0.006 over 1 with the default start and riskier; 4 beat 3 by +0.022. Use 4 on a GPU, 1 on a CPU.

dead_ends.what: autochart's transcriber on WebGPU under WSL
dead_ends.why: the adapter is lavapipe, software Vulkan on the CPU (1031 s against 319 s on CUDA); the transcriber is pinned to the requested device
the stems came out 1105 samples (the encoder delay) late; separate the decoded array

M4-01: torch 2.14.1+cu126 with allin1's torchaudio 2.11.1+cpu is untested on a real cu126 environment (too big for the dev disk); a cpu stand-in passed. Run allin1's probe once in M4-08 or on any machine with room.

DESIGN.md has not yet absorbed M4's orders (wave 1's lanes, doctor and device rows of §2.0 and §4, the VRAM note; M4-03's install; M4-10's §2.15 is in): each order's report in docs/reports/ lists its edits; fold them in with M4-07's doc pass at the latest.
M4-02: doctor does not count a missing torch or demucs as a problem, and the guitar's reason is 'no GPU' on the cpu lane even when a GPU is present (both per the spec's wording).

M4-10: the install (runtime.step_pipeline_models) does not fetch the lyrics weights (1.26 GB): the first --lyrics run downloads them. Fetching them at install is the owner's call (install size and time).

M4-10: lyrics in a script other than Latin get no romanization: such words are spread between their neighbours. The English bundle collapses on a vocal stem as poor as a full mix (warned: median word score under 0.25). Not run on CUDA, nor checked in Clone Hero itself (M4-08 should look at the lyrics display).
M4-10: doctor (device.py) does not list torchaudio among the components, and NOTICE (M4-07) needs torchaudio (BSD-2-Clause) and the wav2vec 2.0 weights (MIT).

A personal-details check in CI (packaging/ci, like check_no_audio.py): emails and home or profile paths in the diff and docs/reports/. The names it should look for can't be written in the public repository: keep them in a CI secret or a file outside it. (pipeline review 2026-11-04, finding 6)
Stall detection by log: builders tee long commands to a progress log with a DONE marker, watched by a Monitor; the heavy-job lock's .who file covers part of it. (pipeline review, finding 9)
Builder effort: try one fully specified order with sc-builder at high instead of xhigh, and compare the review's findings. (pipeline review, finding 4)

DESIGN.md: split by area into docs/design/ (stages, evaluation, packaging, milestones), each headed 'as of <commit>'; move the changelog preamble and §11 to history and §9 to a dated decisions log. With task 41's fold-in of waves 1-2 and M4-10, at M4-07's doc pass at the latest. (pipeline review, finding 11)

The dev machine's allin1 Python (research/timing/venv2) was made by hand and reads torch from the main environment; packaging/allin1 is the supported way, untested as the golden charts' sections backend (its torch build may move the sections' hashes). eval/README.md, 'Rebuilding the dev machine', step 4.
The separation cache was filled by a script never committed (eval/README.md's step 7 stands in for it): a `--stems` maker in eval/golden.py or a small eval script would make it reproducible.
M4-04: song.ogg is not byte-identical between runs of one song (each Ogg page's serial number and checksum; the audio is identical). Pre-existing; the chart and song.ini are byte-identical.

M4-04: the page's WSL paths (the self-check with curl.exe, the NAT fallback, explorer.exe, the shortcut's ui --from-shortcut) are tested with stand-ins only; M4-08 checks them (its 'Added at M4-04's merge').
M4-10: words in a script the aligner can't spell, before the first word it can, collect at that word's start (a text with no spelled word at all gets no lyrics and a warning).

M4-06: the install into Songs on Windows (copy and renames on drvfs, the retries while OneDrive or antivirus holds a folder, a OneDrive-moved Documents, explorer.exe paths, the zip in Downloads) is tested with stand-ins only; M4-08 checks them ('Added at M4-06's merge').
M4-06: a copy into Songs that stopped before song.ini and report.json lacks our marks, so its .tmp folder is left; whether Clone Hero lists dot-folders is unknown until M4-08.
M4-06 decision (the builder's, kept at review): a chart that failed its gate is never installed or exported; its Done screen still shows the preview.

M4-05: an offline reinstall rebuilds songcharter's wheel from uv's cache; it passed minutes after the install, untested days later when uv's cached index has gone stale (nothing promises an offline reinstall).

process_notes: 2026-11-03: a four-lens re-review of merged wave 1 (10 agents) found 3 real findings, all minor, none of them major, after the single-reviewer process; 2 of the 3 were checks whose tests could be gutted. Decision: keep one reviewer per order, with a mutation pass on new checks (.claude/agents/sc-reviewer.md step 3), and the full workflow once over the integrated v0.1.

2026-11-04: an advisor on a different, more capable model reviewed the process (docs/reports/pipeline-review.md): 12 findings. Done: the heavy-job lock in code (tools/heavy.sh, eval/golden.py), M4-10's brief committed as a work order with the lyrics exception, in_flight kept from an order's start, the dev machine's rebuild recipe and the golden baseline committed, a one-hour cache for the roles, the review workflow routing only majors to a skeptic, a disk note at each merge, DESIGN's superseded native plan marked. Deferred: the CI personal-details check, stall logs, a builder-effort trial, DESIGN's split, the planner change (from M5). Declined: model aliases in the agent files, since model identifiers stay out of the repository; the orchestrator names the model at each start.
2026-11-04: in a cloud session with several repositories, .claude/settings.json's permission rules and hooks don't load (only its plugin keys), so rules that must hold live in code or CI.

2026-11-04: the machine restarted mid-run (about 01:29 UTC): /dev/shm and every process went, including two golden checks and their old checkouts; the worktrees, commits and scratch survived. Keep anything a later step needs out of /dev/shm.

On a smaller plan (the owner usually has one; about a tenth of the current plan's weekly use, a 5-hour window, the most capable model on usage credits only): the orchestrator builds small changes itself; one reviewer on a smaller model, for the charting path and the installer only; CI as the inspection; no workflows; a fresh session per order, with PROGRESS as the handoff. Not needed while the current plan lasts (the owner, 2026-11-04).

2026-11-04, M4-10: the reference charts in the dev container have their lyrics stripped, so the builder fetched the original packages again (the same Chorus Encore URLs) into memory to read the lyric events' timings, under the owner's exception; nothing with word text was written to disk, and a scan after the build found none. The review's F2 (non-Latin lyrics all at 0:00) was a major finding sent straight to the fixer, who reproduced it before fixing: the reviewer had shown it with the real engine and the fix cost less than a skeptic.
